Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo — follow-up items

Camila / Ben —

Thanks for the demo earlier. A quick recap from my side and a few clarifying questions so we can move procurement and architecture review forward: 

Summary of key concerns we raised:
- Data residency: PHI must remain inside our VA-managed cloud region (us-west-2). No cross-region backups without explicit consent.
- Network isolation: For the pilot we require a VPC deployment fronted by our NAT/gateway and strict egress rules; ideally a private endpoint inside our subnet.
- Air-gap possibility: If the security team decides, we may need an air-gapped on-prem option for certain workloads (R&D model training outputs).
- Auditability: We need request-level audit logs and retention for 7 years (regulatory).

Immediate asks from Galaxy: 
1) A short doc describing how Redwood enforces network peering, NAT traversal, and whether a private endpoint (no public IP) is supported.
2) A filled security questionnaire (attached) — we've started it and will return by EOD Friday.
3) An estimated T-shirt cost for a pilot (50 req/s sustained, 3B token/month) and what changes for an on-prem air-gap.

Next steps we expect:
- Redwood to provide the network handoff checklist and a contact for infra (we will share our infra engineer).
- Procurement to be looped once the SOC/audit answers are clear.

I'll attach the partially filled questionnaire for your reference.

Lena
Director, Cloud Security
Galaxy Health

--

Thanks Lena — great call and appreciate the clear priority list. Below is a concise post-call recap from our side and the asks we can action this week.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary requirement: VPC-hosted inference in us-west-2 with strict egress controls and no outbound public IPs for pilot.
- Regulatory driver: HIPAA + internal retention policy → 7-year audit logs.
- Contingency: Air-gapped on-prem for particularly sensitive workloads is a probable gating item for the first tranche.
- Pilot target: 50 req/s sustained, expected peak bursts to 80 req/s, ~3B tokens/month baseline.

What Redwood will deliver by end of week (owners):
- Network handoff checklist + sample VPC endpoint diagram (Camila) — includes subnet/route table/NAT recommendations.
- Short note on private endpoint support and how we avoid public IPs (Ben) — includes supported architectures: Private ENI + customer NAT, VPN, and Direct Connect options.
- Security questionnaire answers (Monica) — we'll return a redlined copy in the attached XLSX.
- Pilot cost estimate and an on-prem air-gap delta (Camila + Ben) — high-level numbers and assumptions.

Questions for Galaxy (please confirm):
- Can your infra team accept a peered VPC and/or a PrivateLink endpoint, or do you require VPN/Direct Connect only?
- Is the 7-year retention a hard requirement for all request logs or only for specific audit IDs?
- Do you have an internal deadline for procurement to sign PO / SOW (ballpark date)?

Assignees + next checkpoints:
- Camila: network checklist & pilot cost by Thu EOD (11 May -> actually Thu is 13 May, but we'll deliver 13 May EOD)
- Ben: private endpoint support note by Thu EOD
- Monica: completed questionnaire and SOC references by Thu EOD
- Lena/Rajiv: share your infra contact and expected procurement timeline by Fri 14 May

Attachments sent: galaxy-network-handoff-v1.pdf — diagram stub and preliminary checklist.

If anything above looks off, flag and I'll update. Otherwise we'll proceed to the deeper technical note and cost sheet.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Post-call: Galaxy Health - compliance-driven hosting requirements & network constraints

Camila / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the PDF. A few clarifications from infra/security after internal sync: 

Technical clarifications we need before procurement progress: 
- Connectivity preference: Galaxy prefers Direct Connect for prod but will accept a PrivateLink peering for pilot. We will need the IP ranges (CIDR) you expect to allocate inside our peered VPC.
- Egress controls: All egress must be through our NAT/firewall; outbound TLS is permitted only to Redwood-managed update endpoints (list to be provided).
- Secrets/KMS: We need confirmation that customer-managed KMS keys can be used for model artifacts and logs at rest.
- Audit logs: Will Redwood provide immutable append-only logs exportable to our S3 with lifecycle policies? If so, how is access controlled?

Procurement timeline: aiming to have SOW signed by June 3 if technical clarifications are addressed this week — procurement@galaxyhealth.com will need the cost estimate and a draft SOW.

Action items from Galaxy this week:
- We'll return the completed questionnaire by Fri EOD (Lena).
- Infra will share a point-of-contact and Direct Connect ASN details by Thu EOD.

Camila — if you can confirm the CIDR ranges and KMS approach in the next 24 hours that will help unblock procurement.

Rajiv Mehta
VP Infrastructure, Galaxy Health
